about: A podcast of a grandmother’s stories

lines.text: My classmate Farah has always loved listening to her grandmother talk about the
past. Last December, she decide to record these stories before they were forgotten.
lines.note: Tense: 'last December' is in the past, so it is 'decided'.

lines.text: Using only a phone and a cheap microphone, she began a podcast for hers
lines.note: Pronoun: before a noun ('family') it is 'her', not 'hers'.

lines.text: family. In each episode, her grandmother describes a different part of her childhood,
such as washing clothes at a public tap or sell cakes to neighbours.
lines.note: Verb form: it matches 'washing' — 'washing … or selling'.

lines.text: Farah edits every recording herself, who takes her about three hours. At first,
lines.note: 'Who' is for people. The editing takes 'which'.

lines.text: only her cousins listened. Then a teacher shared the link with the whole
school, and the episodes was soon heard in many other homes. Some listeners
lines.note: Agreement: 'the episodes' is plural, so it is 'were'.

lines.text: have written to say that the stories remind them about their own grandparents.
lines.note: Preposition: something 'reminds you of' a person.

lines.text: Farah’s grandmother, who is eighty, finds all this attention rather amused. She says
lines.note: Word form: the attention is 'amusing'; a person feels 'amused'.

lines.text: her life was ordinary, so Farah believes ordinary lives are worth remembering too.
lines.note: Connector: Farah disagrees, so it is 'but', not 'so'.

lines.text: She plans to keep recording for as long as the stories last.
